systems: util-linux findmnt -o OPTIONS reports the options the kernel holds for the live mount (/proc/self/mountinfo), the only place a forced cifs uid/gid is visible — the fstab line and the declaration are claims, not state
Linux cifs (fs/smb/client) show_options always prints uid=, gid=, file_mode=0%ho and dir_mode=0%ho, so a missing one is not a default

Linux tmpfs omits uid=0, gid=0 and mode=1777 from its options because they are the defaults (shmem_show_options), and umount(8) -l detaches a busy mount lazily, which is why the remount path refuses it
crux.verdict: CHANGELOG-worthy behaviour change: a mount whose ownership options drift is now RED and is remounted, or fails loudly when busy. Nothing else changes for a mount that declares no ownership option.
